utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, sir, we had nothing to do with the combat forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was not whether you something to do with it, but whether you knew it. And your answer is simply no. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 09562.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, there were also RS MUP units on the Trnovo front; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you take RS to mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Republika Srpska, sir.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in Trnovo, there was a police staff. This is the first time I have seen this piece of paper, and you can see that Savo Cvjetinovic, whom I know, was the head of that staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, stop -- stop you again. Were there also RS MUP units on the Trnovo front? If you know, tell us; if you don't know, tell us as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the basis of this paper I can see that they were present there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not asking to interpret a document. That document is shown to you, perhaps, but the question is: Were they there? If you know tell us; if you don't know, tell us as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, Mr. Orie, but you must allow me to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- formulate my answer in a couple of sentences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. You are only allowed to answer the questions and not tell us what you would say on a question that was not put to you. Mr. Traldi. Yes, by the way, we'd like to have an answer still, because I've asked you now three times. Where there also RS MUP units at the Trnovo front?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the minister of the interior deploys the units. I don't know where the units were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was his sole authority to decide where the units would be deployed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again -- I'm not talking about authority. I can imagine of three answers: Yes, they were there; no, they were not there; or I don't know. Which of the three is it? Irrespective of who sent them there, whatever happened, whose authority it was, is it a yes; is it a no; or is it I don't know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume that they were there. I'm not trying to evade this, Mr. Orie.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what's the basis for your assumption?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's because special police brigade units and special police units mainly participated in helping the army wherever there was an offensive. Trnovo was a location where every two or three month there was large-scale combat. I assume, I believe this is the case, that Ministry of Interior units co-operated with the Republika Srpska army because they were present in all battlefields. But as to whether it was the 2nd or 3rd Company or special police brigade, I really could not say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the answer is: Yes, but I do not know what specific units. I see you nodding yes. That's hereby on the record. Why don't you tell us this immediately? Why don't you tell us: What units exactly there were, I do not know, but I know that such units were there? Mr. Traldi will now put his next question and you're invited to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Orie, I said that this was my assumption. I nodded in the sense that wanted to indicate that it was my assumption, as I have already said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now in the tenth line down on the B/C/S, sir, we read that part of the defence line is held by the Skorpions and then it says "MUP Serbia." You mentioned a few moments ago you knew was a unit in Djeletovci called the Skorpions. You -- does this refresh your recollection as to whether that was a MUP Serbia unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Traldi. No. I know of the existence of the Skorpions. I read it about it in print. For about 15 years there was Skorpions in existence, but as to being able to confirm that they were in the Trnovo area, I can't confirm this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to interrupt you --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's probably 90 per cent certain. You probably have a paper to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to interrupt you and ask you again to try to answer my question. Does this, yes or no, refresh your recollection as to whether the Skorpions were under the control of MUP Serbia as Mr. Cvjetinovic writes here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer such a question. I can't answer such a question. How am I to know whether they were there or not? If you had asked me with my own men, I would have said they were under my authority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The simple answer is: It doesn't refresh my recollection. That's apparently the gist of what you say. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So do I understand correctly that the National Security Sector of the Republika Srpska, when its attention was focused on a particular theatre, it could miss the entry of affiliated forces? It wouldn't be aware of what organisations those forces were affiliated with even if it exchanged information on a daily basis with that other organisation? That's the level of intelligence work you're telling me the National Security Sector of the Republika Srpska did?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's quite right. I had no information as to whether they were there or not. Our people didn't focus on the situation of the army and the police. They focused on the situation as regards the lines. That's one matter. And the time we are speaking about is July. There was already an offensive in Glamoc, Visoko, Krajina, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three days after the appearance of this paper --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think you've answered my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I tender the last two documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 09562 receives Exhibit Number P7588, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 06767 receives Exhibit Number P7589, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, sticking with events in July 1995, do I correctly understand from your Karadzic testimony that your evidence is you didn't know about the massacres in Srebrenica until the year 2000?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P7025.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is an article by Robert Block published in the London Independent on the 17th of July, 1995, titled: "Bodies pile up in horror of Srebrenica." He starts by referring to a videocamera panning across the ground in front of a building, then refers to what initially appear to be bundles of abandoned belongings. But then in third paragraph the reporter says there are many dead Muslim soldiers. He says this is was a report by the independent Serb television channel, Studio B, and that the scene looked like a place of summary execution. Did you miss this information when it was published about 2.000 kilometres away on the 17th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I have to say that in my statement I said that from the 14th to the 18th I was at my deputy's wedding. I wasn't in the area of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not at the moment inviting you to repeat your statement. Did you miss the information on the 17th of July? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any such information. With your leave, Mr. Traldi, may I say something else, one more sentence? With your leave, I would like to say the following. Studio B as in the interrogation with -- or examination with [indiscernible], I didn't which film was concerned. I heard about the Studio B making this recording public. It was confiscated later on. But Studio B is a media company that can only broadcast in the area of the Belgrade municipality, so the broadcast can't be received elsewhere in Serbia. I was in Montenegro at the wedding, so I couldn't have been informed about such things at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I understand you claim you were in Montenegro. Do you also claim that when you got back nobody was talking about a video published just a few dozen kilometres away, broadcast just a few dozen kilometres away, showing huge numbers of dead Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Few dozen kilometres away. Belgrade is not a few dozen kilometres away. If it's local station it's crucial --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll defer to Mr. Lukic on the distance, I think. Perhaps for efficiency, I'll simply move to the next document. Can we have 65 ter 33169.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's just a blank white page apparently which is under this number.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think we've just released it, Your Honour, and I apologise for the delay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Give it another try, Madam Registrar, since it's released now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What apparently -- no, we now have -- at least I see on other screens around me, not all the screens are giving the same image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It appeared in e-court instead of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's on some our of screens. Life is not always fair to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I can summarise the essential part for efficiency, Your Honours. Looking at the ninth paragraph in the middle of the first column, we read that a group of Bosnian Serb special police forces under the command of Ljubisa Borovcanin had been responsible for some of the executions. We read about a video and we see that "the Bosnian Serbs in Pale have tried to have it confiscated."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Is it your evidence that on 22nd of July, when the Studio B video had been shown on Belgrade TV, when it had made it to coverage in North American newspapers who were reporting on executions allegedly committed by forces including RS MUP forces, and when the Bosnian Serbs in Pale were trying to have the video confiscated, you still somehow managed to avoid learning about the executions? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Bosnian Serbs from Pale, I don't know who they are. That's the first thing. It certainly wasn't me or my service. We didn't have such information on the 22nd. And on the 25th, I was already in the Krajina area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So your answer is, yes, you somehow missed the information again on the 22nd; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't receive such information. If I had received such information, I probably wouldn't have missed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you did know in 1996 that witnesses -- early 1996 that witnesses before this Tribunal had already at that time described executions of large numbers of Muslim men and boys; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I see the time. I wonder, just to complete this line, if I might have two minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm looking at the interpreter's booth, whether -- yes, there's a thumbs-up for your suggestion, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P3355.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you recognise your signature here on the first page, right, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, Mr. Traldi, the P number as transcribed, we haven't reached 3300 yet. Can you repeat the number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: 3355, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you recognise your name and signature here on the first page; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 2, the third paragraph from the bottom in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see references to two witnesses in The Hague who had made statements that they were present at the time the VRS shot civilians in Srebrenica. So by 1996, you did know, didn't you, that witnesses before this Tribunal were already at that time describing the executions; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you enlarge the paragraph, zoom in on the paragraph, please. Mr. Traldi, this is a text from the IFOR source. Is that what we are referring to. An IFOR base in Dubrave near Tuzla, is that the part you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's the paragraph after that, I take it, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] It is. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you be so kind as to zoom in, please. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you agree now that did you know this in 1996; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is information from the State Security Department that I received, and I just conveyed it to the Ministry of Justice, which at the time had started having contact with The Hague representatives. But this isn't the only paragraph that is in question. There is a paragraph that precedes it. I would like you to read it out as well. It's not just a matter of an investigation. This is something that we received from other sources cooperating with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I didn't put to you that it was an investigation, certainly. What I put to you was you knew witnesses were saying it, you denied it. I understand you've now corrected that. And that completes my questions on the document. With one exception, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we just see the end.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not denying this. All I am saying is that this was alleged. I provided information that such things were being done, but I didn't have any concrete information. Information has to be verified. There were rumours. There were rumours, I don't deny that. But this information arrived on my desk from associates or collaborators among the Muslims. It says what it says, and I don't cast doubt on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the last thing you write -- or the last paragraph you write begins: "We are sending you this information believing that it could be used for the defence." And that was your priority on hearing that there were allegations that the VRS and MUP forces had massacred thousands of defenceless people. Your priority was to get information to the Ministry of Justice so a defence could be organised; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look, at the time, people spoke about Srebrenica. There were rumours. They started performing exhumations. We sent this to the Ministry of Justice that then established initial contact with Ms. Louise Arbour. Naturally, we wanted to clarify matters because in an earlier part of the document it says that one of the commanders killed 30 men, 30 people, and eyewitnesses made statements to such an effect. I wasn't aware of that, and I cannot make such a claim now. An operative drafted this, and we relayed the information. Let's have a look at the first paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, if Mr. Lukic wants to show that you on re-direct, he is welcome to. We'll explore your attempts to clarify matters before the Tribunal more tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: For now, I appreciate everyone's indulgence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kijac, we'll adjourn for the day. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30. And I again instruct you that you should not speak or communicate with whomever about your testimony, whether already given or whether still to be given. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and we resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 22nd of October, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 22nd day of October, 2015, at 9.30 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
